newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm despite political turmoil.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm despite political turmoil.

text.p: Istanbul shares ended higher on Wednesday after fluctuating in a tight range as the market continued to watch political developments closely, brokers said.

Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said he would meet President Suleyman Demirel later today, apparently to submit his resignation under a power-sharing deal with his conservative, pro-Western coalition partner, the True Path Party (DYP).
He had previously agreed to hand over power to DYP leader and deputy PM Tansu Ciller to form a caretaker government to seek early polls by the end of 1997.
Ciller also told a joint news conference with Erbakan that the year-old government would "shortly" come to an end.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed at 1,565, up 14 points, or 0.9 percent from Tuesday after moving between 1,551 and 1,586 in the day.
Trade volume edged up to 13.86 trillion lira from Tuesday's 12.92 trillion.

"There were buying and selling waves depending on political news and expectations that emerged in the day. The prospect of a new government is uncertain. This blocks serious purchases," said Hakan Aksoy from Alfa securities.
"It is also futile to expect healthy movements in the market when early polls are seen in the medium-term," he added.

Ciller also told reporters that the coalition partners secured the support of an eight-member, rightist party with a key position in parliament to back efforts to pass the power transfer and an early election law.
The coalition has been unravelling under pressure from the secularist military and establishment since February.

Of the 242 shares traded, 97 advanced, 66 declined and 79 were steady. The IMKB Industrial .XUSIN firmed 0.82 percent to 1,477, IMKB Services .XUHIZ leapt 2.53 percent to 1,583 and the IMKB Financial .XUMAL firmed 0.65 percent to 1,700.

Leading actives were utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 7,500 lira at 212,500, T.Isbank's C series shares, up 1,000 lira at 45,000 and largely state-owned oil refiner Tupras, up 2,000 lira at 73,000. They made up 29.4 percent of the total turnover.
